name: UCEPROTECT-Network DNSBL (dnsbl-1/2/3.uceprotect.net)
tier_rationale: Long-running DNSBL operator with public documentation and policies (A8 community).

reliability.justification: Level 1 lists single IPs; Levels 2 and 3 list whole allocations and ASNs (escalation), never evidence against a single IP.

level1.title: UCEPROTECT Level 1 (single IPs, dnsbl-1.uceprotect.net)

terms.quote: P045 cond 2 (binding council text): URIBL, SURBL, UCEPROTECT and Barracuda are noncommercial/fair-use lists: off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (their free-use terms recorded and allowed by legal).

level1.notes: Quote: binding council text (P045 cond 2). Answers public resolvers (test point 127.0.0.2 seen 2026-11-25). Only Level 1 counts (P045 cond 7). Off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared. Used by dnsbl.
level1.licensed_alternative: A licence_allow entry recording UCEPROTECT's terms (SpamCop and DroneBL keep running).

level2.title: UCEPROTECT Level 2 (whole allocations, dnsbl-2.uceprotect.net)

terms.quote: P045 cond 2 (binding council text): URIBL, SURBL, UCEPROTECT and Barracuda are noncommercial/fair-use lists: off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (their free-use terms recorded and allowed by legal).

level2.notes: Quote: binding council text (P045 cond 2). Neighbourhood listing: at most info, zero risk (P045 cond 7). Used by dnsbl.
level2.licensed_alternative: A licence_allow entry recording UCEPROTECT's terms.

level3.title: UCEPROTECT Level 3 (whole ASNs, dnsbl-3.uceprotect.net)

terms.quote: P045 cond 2 (binding council text): URIBL, SURBL, UCEPROTECT and Barracuda are noncommercial/fair-use lists: off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared (their free-use terms recorded and allowed by legal).

level3.notes: Quote: binding council text (P045 cond 2). Neighbourhood listing: at most info, zero risk (P045 cond 7). Used by dnsbl.
level3.licensed_alternative: A licence_allow entry recording UCEPROTECT's terms.

notes: Owned by batch p2-G02-2 (P045). DNS only: the list is queried through DNS A lookups (core DoH layer or the system resolver), never over HTTP, so the provider has no HTTP host. Every DNSBL counts as ONE 'spam' family vote in P171 consensus (upstream_family 'dnsbl', P045 cond 8).
